newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNAGFA denounces airlines surcharge imposition.
newsitem.headline: SNAGFA denounces airlines surcharge imposition.

text.p: France's association of air freight forwarding agents, SNAGFA, said the way surcharges on freight had been applied, to cover rising jet fuel costs, was totally "unacceptable."
Lufthansa had imposed a 50 centimes per kilo surcharge from November 1 and Air France and KLM by the same amount from November 4 on "all products and destinations," a SNAGFA statement said.

"The surcharges amount to unilatereal action by the airlines in question and were applied without any consulation whatsoever with agents and shippers which we vigorously deplore," SNAGFA general secretary, Bruno Charrois, told Reuters.
He said SNAGFA had very close working relations with Air France but news of the surcharges had come as a complete surprise to agents.

"Just a week ago, we were in contact with Air France but there was not an inkling of any surcharges in the pipline. Our members were left with the task of notifying thousands of customers at short notice which frankly, in the modern distribution trade, is no way to do business."
SNAGFA had requested airlines postpone the application of the surcharges until the outcome of "real and genuine dialogue between the different parties concerned in the air cargo industry."

The surcharges worked out at an approximately ten percent increase on ex-Paris rates on Transatlantic routes which was significant addition to shippers transport costs in one fell swoop, Charrois added.

"Beyond lobbying for a postponement, we can't say at this moment in time what action we plan to take in protest to the surcharges because the full impact of the airlines decision is still sinking in. However, there will be a determined riposte."
